text: From spring 2025 the Russian 20th Combined Arms Army pushed a salient into the ground north of Lyman, between the Nitrius and Zherebets rivers.

The aim of the Russian salient north of Lyman was to bypass Lyman from the north, reach Sviatohirsk and the Siverskyi Donets, and form the northern pincer of an envelopment of the Donetsk fortress belt (Sloviansk, Kramatorsk, Druzhkivka, Kostiantynivka).

text: In DeepState's polygons, the Russian-occupied area in a 1,096 km² box around the Lyman salient grew from 60 km² on 1 March 2025 to 350 km² on 15 January 2026.
Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps under Brig. Gen. Andrii Biletskyi first stabilised the line north of Lyman and stopped the Russian infiltration before attacking.
Under "maximum information silence", the 3rd Army Corps attacked the northern flank of the Lyman salient at Nove, with the first visible attack on 22 May 2026.
Before and during the Operation Vivaldi ground attacks the 3rd Army Corps ran a drone and EW campaign that blinded Russian drones and hit Rubikon's operators and launch sites.
During Operation Vivaldi the 3rd Army Corps struck Russian logistics first 50 km and then 120 km deep.
During Operation Vivaldi the 3rd Army Corps cut a diesel pipeline from Voronezh Oblast that supplied Russian forces.
The 3rd Army Corps' first-phase method in Operation Vivaldi was to kill the ATV and motorcycle reinforcements sent to stranded Russian infiltration groups, not to chase every infiltrator.
